scene_translation: The moment you turned the page of the old notebook, your hand froze. In the middle of the pages, written not just dates but a single line: "Tesuto, you will surely come here." The bookshop owner, Tanaka-san, quietly drew near and said in a small voice, "That notebook was left behind by a previous customer. It seems it belonged to the person in the blue coat…" Looking out the window, the woman in blue was still standing there, staring straight at you.
grammar_note: 【〜だけでなく】means "not only … but also." It connects two elements to show that something goes beyond what was first expected: <ruby>日付<rt>ひづけ</rt></ruby>だけでなく、「テスト、<ruby>必<rt>かなら</rt></ruby>ずここに<ruby>来<rt>く</rt></ruby>る」という<ruby>一文<rt>いちぶん</rt></ruby>も<ruby>書<rt>か</rt></ruby>かれていた (Not only dates, but also the line "Tesuto, you will surely come here" was written). Pattern: [noun/verb]だけでなく、[noun/verb]も.

mystery_memo: The notebook now explicitly addresses the player by name ('Tesuto, you will surely come here'), deepening the sense that this mystery was arranged for them specifically. Tanaka the bookshop owner has revealed the notebook was left by the woman in blue — making her the original owner, not merely an observer. The dates matching the grandmother's Tokyo visits remain the key puzzle: the woman in blue may have known the grandmother. Tanaka-san is cooperative and polite (ally), seemingly unaware of the deeper mystery. The woman in blue remains outside — watchful, patient, possibly waiting to make contact.

npcs.note: 古い本屋の店主で、丁寧な話し方をする穏やかな人物。ノートが青いコートの客の忘れ物だと教えてくれた。
